chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man does not enter Makkah with tranquility except that he is forgiven. I said, 'What is the tranquility?' He said, 'Humbleness.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'sakinah' mean in the context of entering Makkah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual state of 'sakinah'—defined here as humility and composure—to the forgiveness of sins upon entering Makkah. This reflects the Shia emphasis on internalizing the etiquette of the pilgrimage, where physical entry is accompanied by a heart purified of arrogance, aligning with the broader theological concept that true reverence for the House of God requires inner tranquility.
